title: Alternate Picking for Beginners: Angle, In/Out Motion, and Downward Pickslanting (JustinGuitar)
summary: This JustinGuitar lesson introduces beginner-friendly alternate picking on single strings, focusing on how the pick’s angle and a deliberate in‑toward/outward motion affect efficiency and speed. The host demonstrates how a flat pick tends to catch and how a slight angle (around 20 degrees) lets the pick glide over the string, then emphasizes a practical in‑toward/outward motion (about 45 degrees) to ease string crossings. The video also presents the concept of Downward Pickslanting, credits Troy Grady and his Cracking The Code site, and suggests experimentation with different grips and anchor points (e.g., little finger) while keeping the practice goal simple: just alternate picking on one string to develop feel and control. Aimed at beginners, the lesson blends technique tips with a clear, patient practice plan and points to further resources for faster picking.

sections.title: Tip 2 - In & Out with the Pick
sections.description: The video demonstrates that a flat pick catches on the string and slows movement. By angling the pick slightly away from flat, the pick glides more smoothly, enabling faster, cleaner motion. The host recommends a small angle (around 20 degrees) as a practical starting point and notes typical pick visibility for teaching clarity.
